title: KV warmth signal onboarding checklist
content:
Context and goal:
This doc is a compact onboarding checklist and working playbook for instrumenting and onboarding KV-cache warmth signals for tokenized inference flows. The aim is to create a low-noise, actionable metric surface that helps operators and engineers quickly answer: is the cache healthy, who is cold, and why did latency spike? This is a pragmatic working doc — expect TODOs and short-form notes.

Why KV-warmth matters (short):
- KV warmth (aka prefix/KV cache hitfulness) is one of the largest levers on per-token latency and cost.
- Small numbers of cold tenants or high eviction churn can cause outsized tail latency and token-cost regressions.
- We need signals that are robust to noisy multi-tenant traffic, and that map to investigation steps.

High-level signal taxonomy (recommended):
- kv.request_count: count of requests that touched the KV cache boundary (string tag: model, tenant, route).
- kv.kv_hits: count of requests where the cache provided a hit for at least one prefix/KV lookup.
- kv.kv_hit_rate (derived): kv.kv_hits / kv.request_count (windows: 1m, 5m, 1h).
- kv.per_tenant_warmth: moving-window hit_rate per tenant (p95 and p50 windows, min sample size guard).
- kv.evictions: number of entries evicted (tags: node, reason=e.g. ttl/size/compaction).
- kv.kv_latency_ms: latency contribution for KV path (histogram).
- kv.prefix_cold_tail_fraction: fraction of requests with cold prefix events that triggered long token tails (>350ms extra).

Metric definitions and decimals/units:
- kv.request_count: integer counter, unit = requests.
- kv.kv_hits: integer counter. Tag cardinality restriction: model, region, tenant_bucket (see below).
- kv.kv_hit_rate: percent, report as decimal 0.0-1.0 and % on dashboards.
- kv.evictions: integer counter with reason tag.
- kv.kv_latency_ms: histogram buckets: [0, 1, 5, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000] ms.

Tagging & cardinality guidance (must follow):
- High-card tags allowed: model (capped to top-50 active models).
- Tenant tagging: do NOT use full tenant_id for dashboards unless in investigation context. Create tenant_bucket tag: {top10, mid, longtail} computed via monthly_token_volume. Use per-tenant detailed traces only when investigating.
- Node id and pool_type tag allowed for backend dashboards; avoid exposing unique instance ids in high-card widgets.

Dashboard composition suggestions (layout):
1) Global overview row (1m/5m): kv.request_count (rate), kv.kv_hit_rate (1m, 5m), kv.kv_latency_ms p50/p95/p99
2) Eviction & churn row: kv.evictions by reason, eviction_rate per node pool, p95 kv_latency for eviction-heavy nodes
3) Tenant-weighted warmth row: per_tenant_warmth (top10 tenants by token volume), longtail warmth histogram, anomaly sparklines for sudden drops
4) Investigation row: prefix_cold_tail_fraction over last 1h, sample of example request ids (linked to trace explorer), synthetic probe results (see synthetic section)

Widget heuristics to reduce noise:
- Smooth per-tenant curves with a 5m EWMA; show raw thin line + smoothed thick line.
- Only display per-tenant lines for top10 by token volume by default; provide dropdown to expand.
- For heatmaps, limit axis cardinality and bucket tenants into the tenant_bucket tag.

Tracing guidance & anchor spans:
- Span design: add a top-level span kv-cache.lookup that contains tags: model, tenant_bucket, prefix_shard, hit=true/false, entry_count, eviction_flag. Duration should measure only the KV lookup code path.
- Add child span kv-cache.fetch-mem and kv-cache.fetch-remote as needed.
- Place a trace-anchor (string) in long-running requests when cold path is detected: attr cold_reason = "eviction_ttl" | "cold_start" | "prefix_miss".
- Sampling: prefer severity-weighted sampling: always keep traces where kv.kv_latency_ms > 100ms OR where kv.kv_hit_rate < 0.2 for tenant_bucket=top10. For longtail tenants, sample probabilistically at 0.1%.
- Correlate traces with synthetic probe ids (probe_id) so synthetic runs can surface a representative trace.

Synthetic probes and canaries (recommended):
- Run a per-region synthetic job that executes a representative set of prefixes (short convo beginnings and large context warmups) every 30s. Record: probe_id, model, expected_hit_rate, observed_hit_rate, lat_p95, trace_id.
- Use synthetic probes to seed baselines per model: if synthetic probe p95 latency jumps > 30% or observed_hit_rate drops > 15% vs baseline, auto-create an alert (see alerts).

Alerting thresholds (starter suggestions):
- Critical: global kv.kv_hit_rate (5m) < 0.4 AND kv.kv_latency_ms p95 > 300ms => page on-call.
- High: synthetic probe p95 increase > 30% OR synthetic observed_hit_rate delta < -15% for 3 consecutive runs => notify #obs and create incident-draft.
- Medium: eviction_rate per node pool > baseline + 3 sigma for 10m => notify on-call rota (email/async).

Investigation playbook (priority steps):
1) Check global overview dashboard: is the hit_rate drop global or tenant-limited?
2) If tenant-limited: open tenant detail (use tenant_bucket) and inspect per_tenant_warmth sparkline and last traces.
3) If global: check recent deployments (linked_artifacts above), autoscaler events, and node pool eviction spikes.
4) Trace sampling: fetch recent traces with anchor cold_reason != null. Inspect suffix to see where token tail latency originates.
5) Reproduce with synthetic probe if necessary. Attach probe trace_id to incident.
6) If root cause is eviction churn: collect heap snapshots, examine ttl policies, and propose temporary increase in cache size for affected pool.

Quick query examples (pseudo-SQL / metrics DSL):
- per_tenant_warmth(past_1h) = sum(kv.kv_hits{tenant_bucket=$tb} by tenant) / sum(kv.request_count{tenant_bucket=$tb} by tenant)
- eviction_spike = increase(kv.evictions[5m]) / increase(kv.request_count[5m])
- cold_tail_fraction = sum(kv.prefix_cold_tail_fraction{region=$r}) by instance_pool

Data quality and guardrails:
- Minimum sample size: only compute per_tenant_warmth if request_count >= 50 in that window; otherwise show a low-sample badge.
- Missing metrics fallback: if kv.kv_hits is not present for a node for >10min, mark node as uninstrumented and generate a telemetry health alert.
- Backfill policy: we should not backfill kv.kv_hit_rate from logs — require live instrumenting in code (counter + span tagging).

Operational TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add tenant_bucket enrichment to ingestion pipeline (owner: Mateo)
- [ ] Add kv-cache.lookup span to runtime (owner: Priya, PR: gh:repo/runtime#410)
- [ ] Create synthetic probe job (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Dashboard wireframe + low-noise widgets (owner: Eleanor)
- [ ] Alert runbook steps expanded into OpsPlaybook doc (owner: SRE team)

Open questions / discussion items:
- What is the acceptable warmth baseline per model? (We need model-class-specific baselines; discussion with Applied ML)
- Tenant privacy: what detail can CS see for longtail tenants when investigating? (legal check pending)
- Should we surface per-customer sample traces automatically into CS console for faster debugging?

Notes / references:
- See CON-OBS-1123 for instrumentation standards; link above.
- Slack thread: #infra-kv-caching (thread ts 1701234567.000200) has recent notes about eviction tuning.
- Related dashboards: heatmap templates and probe-runbook in gh:repo/dashboards/templates (PR upcoming).

Quick glossary:
- KV warmth: shorthand for effective cache hitfulness for prefix/KV cache used during autoregressive generation.
- Tenant_bucket: privacy-friendly bucketing of tenants used to limit cardinality.

If you are onboarding a model or tenant, follow this checklist and ping the owners above. Iteration expected — this doc should be trimmed into a short onboarding card for new hires once stable.

End of doc.
